candidate.answerReason: The pictured pattern adds successive layers of 4, 8, 12, … squares. Figure 100 therefore contains 1 + 4(1 + 2 + ⋯ + 100) = 20201 squares.

methods.label: Count the added layers
methods.explanation:
The figures grow by adding a layer around the preceding figure. Counting these separate layers avoids having to draw figure \(100\).

Number the layers outward from the central square. For an integer \(k\geq1\), layer \(k\) consists of the squares exactly \(k\) horizontal or vertical unit steps from the center. It has one top square and one bottom square. In each of the \(2k-1\) rows between them, it has two squares, one on each side. Thus layer \(k\) contains
\[
2+2(2k-1)=4k
\]
squares.

Figure \(n\), for a nonnegative integer \(n\), contains the central square and layers \(1\) through \(n\). Every square belongs to exactly one layer, so none is omitted or counted twice. Its total is therefore
\[
1+4(1+2+\cdots+n).
\]
For \(n=100\), pair \(1\) with \(100\), \(2\) with \(99\), and so on. There are \(50\) pairs, each totaling \(101\), so
\[
1+4(1+2+\cdots+100)
=1+4\cdot50\cdot101
=\boxed{20201}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument derives the growth rule from the pictured layers and evaluates an arithmetic sum by pairing. It uses only elementary counting and algebra.
